OmniCore Host third-party driver distribution

libusbK 3.1.0.0
  Official release: https://github.com/mcuee/libusbk/releases/tag/V3.1.0.0
  Mirror/checksum: https://sourceforge.net/projects/libusbk/files/libusbK-release/3.1.0.0/
  libusbK.sys and libusbK.dll are unmodified official release files.
  The x64 kernel SHA256 is 1df66ff22e2eaec27180756d90926ca5b07e8bcf6b0e4e3c56471e63a3a05fa6.
  The release package/user DLL version is 3.1.0.0; the kernel file's own version resource is
  3.0.7.0. This is how the official release is packaged, not a locally changed driver.
  Copyright Travis Lee Robinson and other named contributors; see libusbK LICENSE and AUTHORS files.
  libusbK components are BSD licensed or dual BSD/GPL, as stated in the included source.
  The compatibility libusb0 DLL is included by libwdi's official INF template and retains its own notices.
  Microsoft WDF coinstaller in the official distribution remains unmodified. Modern Windows normally
  uses its inbox KMDF framework. This package is intended only for Windows 10/11 x64.

libwdi 1.5.1
  https://github.com/pbatard/libwdi/releases/tag/v1.5.1
  Copyright Pete Batard and contributors. GNU LGPL version 3 or later.
  Dynamically loaded by och-driver.exe. The library can be replaced by a compatible rebuilt version.
  Corresponding source is included in sources/libwdi-v1.5.1.zip.
  Local source changes: embedder_files.h uses zero-padded WdfCoInstaller01009.dll filenames for the
  official libusbK 3.1.0.0 bundle. The build script applies this two-line filename patch and generates
  config.h enabling only x64 and libusbK, WDF_VER=1009, and standard logging. No signing logic changed.
  Build with MinGW-w64 GCC using driver-build/build-driver.ps1; extract the official libusbK binary
  distribution under third_party/driver/libusbK-3.1.0.0 and the libwdi source under
  third_party/driver/libwdi-1.5.1 in the project layout shown in that script.
  Replacing/debugging the LGPL library is permitted. No restrictions on reverse engineering for
  debugging LGPL modifications are imposed by this distribution.

MinGW/GCC runtime
  The helper and host use statically linked GCC/MinGW runtime code with its runtime-library exception.
  See mingw/ for GCC and mingw-w64 copyright and license notices.

Installer build tool (not a runtime dependency)
  Inno Setup 6.2.2, https://github.com/jrsoftware/issrc/releases/tag/is-6_2_2
  Copyright Jordan Russell and Martijn Laan. The official installer was signature-verified, and its
  compiler was extracted into the project without installing system associations or changing PATH.
  The tool's license is retained in tools/installer/inno-6.2.2/app/license.txt in the source project.
  innoextract 1.9 (Zlib license), https://github.com/dscharrer/innoextract/releases/tag/1.9,
  was used for release validation only and is not required to rebuild the installer.

Application binaries and setup.exe are currently unsigned. This is independent of the valid
Authenticode signatures on the unmodified kernel driver. No code-signing identity is implied.
